title: VicEdit: Learning to Edit Videos from Visual In-Context Examples
claim: Text-only conditioning causes drift, ambiguity and static outputs; adding visual in-context examples fixes them, unlike auxiliary-branch reference methods.
layout: Top 3-column result grid with input/baseline/ours rows; bottom 3 paradigm diagrams
description: The figure has two halves. The top half is a 3-column grid of video-frame strips, drawn as filmstrips, for style transfer, background change and creative edit. Rows are the input, text-only editing and VicEdit (ours), with a final row of visual in-context examples (single image, image pair, video pair). Red crosses and red boxes label baseline failures: stylistic drift, spatial ambiguity and static dynamics. Green checks and green boxes label ours: coherent textures, spatial coherence and vibrant dynamics. A dashed line separates the top half from the bottom half. The bottom half has three block diagrams of paradigms: (a) text-only, (b) ref-image editing, (c) visual in-context editing (ours). Each shows prompt, source video, MLLM and DiT boxes. Colored arrows mark the added reference inputs: yellow for the reference image, and an orange dashed box of in-context examples for (c). The eye goes first to the vivid edited frames.
caption: Top: Qualitative comparison of VicEdit with text-only baselines. Single-image, imagepair, and video-pair references help mitigate stylistic drift, spatial inaccuracies, and insufficient motion guidance, respectively. Bottom: Video editing paradigms: (a) text-only guidance; (b) visual reference conditioning via auxiliary branches; and (c) VicEdit, which distills modality-aware editing semantics from heterogeneous references and fuses them with text instructions within the video DiT. All examples are from OpenVE [1].
abstract: Despite remarkable progress in instruction-based video editing, textual descriptions remain limited in expressing fine-grained appearance, spatial transformations, and temporal dynamics. We introduce Visual In-context Editing, a new paradigm that shifts video editing from text-only instructions to visual demonstrations, where users specify desired edits through heterogeneous visual references including single images, image pairs, and video pairs. To establish this paradigm, we curate VicEdit-400K, the first large-scale dataset for visual in-context video editing, containing 400K high-quality samples across ten editing tasks with comprehensive semantic and visual consistency filtering. Building upon this foundation, we propose VicEdit, a unified framework that enables effective reasoning over diverse visual contexts and textual instructions. Specifically, we introduce Modality-Adaptive Semantic Distillation to extract modality-aware visual editing semantics and Dual-Context Injection to align visual contexts with textual editing intents. Extensive experiments on VicEdit-Bench demonstrate that VicEdit achieves state-of-the-art performance on both conventional instruction-based editing and visual in-context editing. Further controlled studies and human evaluations verify that VicEdit effectively leverages heterogeneous visual references, establishing visual in-context editing as a promising paradigm for controllable video editing.
